macros.name: alignment
macros.doc: The position of the output can be aligned left, right or centered on the page by \alignment{⟨position⟩} with the ⟨position⟩ parameter left, center or right.

macros.name: alignrightlabels
macros.doc: Names and numbering of the last alignment block can either be displayed right next to the sequences or aligned right with the previous labels: \alignrightlabels (undo with \unalignrightlabels).

macros.name: backtranslabel
macros.doc: the size and style of the nucleotide triplets of backtranslations can be set by ‘\backtranslabel’ and ‘\backtranstext’.

macros.name: bargraphstretch
macros.doc: The plotted bars can be stretched by a factor if the appearance is not as desired: \bargraphstretch[⟨position⟩]{⟨factor⟩}.

macros.name: charstretch
macros.doc: With \charstretch{⟨factor⟩} and \linestretch{⟨factor⟩} the width and height/depth, respectively, of the boxes can be multiplied individually by a ⟨factor⟩ to stretch (> 1) or shrink (< 1) the dimensions.

macros.name: chimeraballScale
macros.doc: For the radius of the α-carbon spheres the logo information bit-value is used, which can be scaled using \chimeraballScale{⟨factor⟩} with ⟨factor⟩ from 0–1.

macros.name: chimerachain
macros.doc: If a 3D structure file contains more than one chain, the structure meme display can be restricted to one chain using \chimerachain{⟨chainlabel⟩} with ⟨chainlabel⟩ typically being a letter e.g. {A}.

macros.name: clearlogocolors
macros.doc: Logo colors can be turned to ‘Black’ with the command \clearlogocolors[⟨color⟩] with the optional parameter not set.

macros.name: DNAsims
macros.doc: With \pepsims and \DNAsims residues are defined which are similar to the consensus residue.

macros.name: dofrequencycorrection
macros.doc: Frequency correction can be turned on by \dofrequencycorrection and off by \undofrequencycorrection.

macros.name: emphdefault
macros.doc: Which style TEXshade uses for emphasizing regions is defined by \emphdefault{⟨style⟩}.

macros.name: englishlanguage
macros.doc: With the commands \germanlanguage, \spanishlanguage and \englishlanguage switching between the languages is made possible.

macros.name: featurerule
macros.doc: The thickness can be generally set by the separate command \featurerule{⟨length⟩} with any TeX measure as ⟨length⟩, e. g. \featurerule{3pt}.

macros.name: fingerprint
macros.doc: The command \fingerprint{⟨res. per line⟩} takes one argument stating the desired number of residues per line, e. g. \fingerprint{1000}.

macros.name: firstcolumnDSSP
macros.doc: One can choose which column will be read by TEXshade by ‘\firstcolumnDSSP’ and \secondcolumnDSSP’.

macros.name: funcgroup
macros.doc: New amino acid groups are defined with the \funcgroup command.

macros.name: funcshadingstyle
macros.doc: In order to exchange the colors but to keep the group definitions and descriptions the command \funcshadingstyle can be employed.

macros.name: gapchar
macros.doc: the symbol which is displayed in sequence gaps is freely selectable with \gapchar{⟨symbol⟩}.

macros.name: gapcolors
macros.doc: The colors of the gaps and gap symbols are set by \gapcolors{⟨symbol color⟩}{⟨background color⟩}.

macros.name: geneticcode
macros.doc: Such files with the suffix .cod can be loaded in the TEXshade environment by \geneticcode{⟨filename⟩}, e. g. \geneticcode{ciliate}.

macros.name: hideallmatchpositions
macros.doc: Since alignment positions where all residues match may not contain much information, those sites can be blanked out using \hideallmatchpositions.

macros.name: hideconsensus
macros.doc: To hide the consensus use \hideconsensus.

macros.name: hidelegend
macros.doc: The commands \showlegend and \hidelegend display or clear the legend at the end of the alignment.

macros.name: hidenames
macros.doc: In order to hide all names or the numbering use the command \hidenames or \hidenumbering.

macros.name: hidenumbering
macros.doc: In order to hide all names or the numbering use the command \hidenames or \hidenumbering.

macros.name: hideresidues
macros.doc: If a very graphical output of the sequences is desired, the residue symbols or letters can be blanked out by \hideresidues.

macros.name: hideruler
macros.doc: A ruler is hidden with \hideruler[⟨top/bottom⟩].

macros.name: hideseq
macros.doc: If one or more sequences from the alignment input file should be used for the calculation of the consensus but it is desired not to display these sequences in the final output use the command \hideseq{⟨seq1⟩,⟨seq2⟩,. . . ,⟨seq n⟩}.

macros.name: hideseqs
macros.doc: When all sequences should be hidden, e.g. to show a sequence logo alone, one can simply say \hideseqs.

macros.name: includeDSSP
macros.doc: Protein secondary structure files in the DSSP, STRIDE and PHD format can be included and displayed automatically within the alignment by ‘\includeDSSP’ (and similar commands for STRIDE, PHDsec and PHDtopo, 4.6.4).

macros.name: killseq
macros.doc: In order to completely exclude sequences the command \killseq{⟨seq1⟩,⟨seq2⟩,. . . ,⟨seq n⟩} is provided.

macros.name: linestretch
macros.doc: With \charstretch{⟨factor⟩} and \linestretch{⟨factor⟩} the width and height/depth, respectively, of the boxes can be multiplied individually by a ⟨factor⟩ to stretch (> 1) or shrink (< 1) the dimensions.

macros.name: memelabelcutoff
macros.doc: To eliminate irrelevant residues a cut-off bit-value can be set \memelabelcutoff{⟨bit-value⟩}.

macros.name: messagePDBlist
macros.doc: In case one needs the position numbers of the selected residues for usage in other applications, those can be either printed in the TeX document with \printPDBlist{⟨selection⟩} or shown during the TeX run with \messagePDBlist{⟨selection⟩}.

macros.name: movelegend
macros.doc: The location can be changed by \movelegend{⟨x-offset⟩}{⟨y-offset⟩}. Both parameters require a TeX length, e. g. \movelegend{5cm}{-2cm} moves the legend 5 cm to the right and 2 cm up.

macros.name: namecolor
macros.doc: In order to change the colors only of some sequence names or numbers the commands \namecolor{⟨seq1⟩, ... ,⟨seq n⟩}{⟨color⟩} and \numbercolor{⟨seq1⟩, ... ,⟨seq n⟩}{⟨color⟩} are provided.

macros.name: nameconsensus
macros.doc: With \nameconsensus{⟨name⟩} any name can be set.

macros.name: namesequencelogo
macros.doc: A name for the sequence logo can be set, which is displayed next to the scale by \namesequencelogo{⟨name⟩}.

macros.name: namesubfamilylogo
macros.doc: a name for the subfamily logo is set by \namesubfamilylogo[⟨neg.name⟩]{⟨pos.name⟩} with a required name for the positive part of the logo and an optional name for the negative part.

macros.name: noblockskip
macros.doc: The vertical space between the sequence blocks can be controlled by the commands \smallblockskip, \medblockskip (default setting), \bigblockskip or \noblockskip.

macros.name: numbercolor
macros.doc: In order to change the colors only of some sequence names or numbers the commands \namecolor{⟨seq1⟩, ... ,⟨seq n⟩}{⟨color⟩} and \numbercolor{⟨seq1⟩, ... ,⟨seq n⟩}{⟨color⟩} are provided.

macros.name: numberingwidth
macros.doc: The reserved space for the sequence numbering is set by the command \numberingwidth{⟨n digits⟩}.

macros.name: orderseqs
macros.doc: The sequence order given by the alignment input file is easily reorganized by \orderseqs{⟨seq1⟩,⟨seq2⟩,. . . ,⟨seq n⟩} without the need for editing the alignment input file (which would be a big copy’n’paste job).

macros.name: pepsims
macros.doc: With \pepsims and \DNAsims residues are defined which are similar to the consensus residue.

macros.name: printPDBlist
macros.doc: In case one needs the position numbers of the selected residues for usage in other applications, those can be either printed in the TeX document with \printPDBlist{⟨selection⟩} or shown during the TeX run with \messagePDBlist{⟨selection⟩}.

macros.name: relevance
macros.doc: In order to better recognize relevant positions in the subfamily logo, a bit-value can be set above which the deviation is considered relevant by the command \relevance{⟨bit-value⟩}.

macros.name: residuesperline
macros.doc: With \residuesperline{⟨number⟩} a new value can be set. If this value exceeds the highest possible number of residues per line it is ignored; lower values are accepted of course.

macros.name: rulerspace
macros.doc: To adjust the distance between the ruler and the top or bottom sequence row use \rulerspace[⟨top/bottom⟩]{⟨length⟩}, e. g. \rulerspace{1mm}.

macros.name: rulersteps
macros.doc: The steps between two numbers are set by \rulersteps[⟨top/bottom⟩]{⟨number⟩}.

macros.name: secondcolumnDSSP
macros.doc: One can choose which column will be read by TEXshade by ‘\firstcolumnDSSP’ and \secondcolumnDSSP’.

macros.name: separationline
macros.doc: This command inserts vertical space after the sequence which is refered to by ⟨seqref⟩.

macros.name: setdomain
macros.doc: This command will display only selected residues in the alignment.

macros.name: setends
macros.doc: The specified sequence is truncated at positions ⟨start⟩ and ⟨stop⟩.

macros.name: setfont
macros.doc: With \setfont{⟨text⟩}{⟨family⟩}{⟨series⟩}{⟨shape⟩}{⟨size⟩} all four font attributes of one ⟨text⟩ can be changed simultaneously.

macros.name: setweight
macros.doc: One can change individual values or even define a new weight table using the command \setweight{⟨res.1⟩}{⟨res.2⟩}{⟨value⟩}, e.g. \setweight{E}{Q}{2} or \setweight{K}{C}{-5}.

macros.name: shadeallresidues
macros.doc: With \shadeallresidues the threshold is ignored and all residues are shaded due to their group assignment.

macros.name: shadeblock
macros.doc: In analogy to \shaderegion which is restricted to a single sequence, \shadeblock shades the corresponding region in all other sequences as well except the consensus.

macros.name: shadingcolors
macros.doc: One can choose from five predefined shading color schemes with the command \shadingcolors{⟨scheme⟩}.

macros.name: shadingmode
macros.doc: You can choose from six shading modes and declare one option which depends on the selected mode.

macros.name: shiftsingleseq
macros.doc: The sequence start position in the first line can be shifted by a certain number of residue positions \shiftsingleseq[⟨num⟩].

macros.name: shortcaption
macros.doc: In order to show a short version of the caption in the ”List of Figures” the \shortcaption{⟨short caption text⟩} command can be used.

macros.name: showfeaturename
macros.doc: Using \showfeaturename will print the name in the same line as the descriptive text of the feature whereas \showfeaturestylename will put the name in the same line as the feature symbols.

macros.name: showfeaturestylename
macros.doc: Using \showfeaturename will print the name in the same line as the descriptive text of the feature whereas \showfeaturestylename will put the name in the same line as the feature symbols.

macros.name: showlegend
macros.doc: The commands \showlegend and \hidelegend display or clear the legend at the end of the alignment.

macros.name: showlogoscale
macros.doc: the bit-scale can be turned off and on using \hidelogoscale and \showlogoscale[⟨color⟩]{⟨position⟩}, respectively, with ⟨position⟩ left, right, or leftright and an optional ⟨color⟩.

macros.name: shownegatives
macros.doc: subfamily logos contain negative values, which can be displayed \shownegatives[⟨weak, medium, strong⟩] or hidden \hidenegatives. Without the optional parameter negative residues will be tinted by 50%, i.e. medium.

macros.name: showsequencelogo
macros.doc: Logos will be shown after the command: \showsequencelogo[⟨colorset⟩]{⟨top/bottom⟩}.

macros.name: showsubfamilylogo
macros.doc: Subfamily logos are displayed analogous to sequence logos by the command \showsubfamilylogo[⟨colorset⟩]{⟨top/bottom⟩} and hidden by \hidesubfamilylogo.

macros.name: similaritytable
macros.doc: A full similarity/identity table showing values for all sequences of the alignment can be set using \similaritytable.

macros.name: smallblockskip
macros.doc: The vertical space between the sequence blocks can be controlled by the commands \smallblockskip, \medblockskip (default setting), \bigblockskip or \noblockskip.

macros.name: stopchar
macros.doc: The character shown at stop positions can be changed by \stopchar{⟨symbol⟩}.

macros.name: structurememe
macros.doc: the command \structurememe[⟨seqref⟩]{⟨filename⟩} generates an Chimera output file (use the ending .cmd or .com) with ⟨seqref⟩ as the reference sequence for which a protein structure file must be available for display.

macros.name: undofrequencycorrection
macros.doc: Frequency correction can be turned on by \dofrequencycorrection and off by \undofrequencycorrection.

macros.name: vblockspace
macros.doc: the command \vblockspace{⟨length⟩} allows one to set a defined space length using any TeX unit, e. g. \vblockspace{0.4in}.

macros.name: weighttable
macros.doc: For calculation of the consensus color shading or for bar graphs or color scales in the \feature lines (4.6.3), a residue weight table can be selected by \weighttable{⟨table⟩} with ⟨table⟩ being identity, structural, PAM250, PAM100, or BLOSUM62 (default is identity).
